newsitem.title: USA: Hertz Corp shares leap after market debut.
newsitem.headline: Hertz Corp shares leap after market debut.

text.p: Shares of Hertz Corp surged after the world's biggest car rental company made its market debut on the New York Stock Exchange.
The stock jumped 4, or nearly 17 percent, to 28, at the opening, and moved slightly higher in early trading, to 28-1/2.

The initial public offering raised more than $400 million for Hertz, a unit of Ford Motor Co. The 17.4 million shares priced at $24 a share on Thursday by lead underwriter J.P. Morgan & Co Inc, the high end of expectations.
Hertz was the most active stock and the highest percent-gainer on the New York Stock Exchange.
Shares of Ford Motor slipped 1/8 to 34-3/8. The U.S. No. 2 automaker is divesting some of Hertz as part of a campaign to unlock value in Ford's non-automotive assets.

Ford now owns more than 50 percent of Hertz's class A shares and all of the Class B shares. According to a regulatory filing, the class B stock has five votes a share, whereas the class A common stock offers one vote a share.
IPO analysts had forecast a stand-out opening performance for Hertz, in contrast to an otherwise sluggish IPO market, which has underperformed the Nasdaq so far in 1997.

Lehman Brothers analyst Jeff Kessler initiated coverage of the stock on Friday with a buy rating, according to a research report. He gave the stock a 12-month price target of $32 and said the stock deserves a higher valuation than the rest of the car rental industry because of its market-leading position.

"Many times we have the cart before the horse with IPOs. Hertz is the horse. It is the leader in its industry, the biggest player. When they make a policy change, everyone else follows it," said David Menlow, president of the IPO Financial Network.
Of the total 20.01 million shares offered, 18.27 million are slated for the United States and Canada, the underwriter said.
Hertz had originally filed for a 17.4 million global share offering with an overallotment option of an additional 2.61 million shares. The price range was $21 to $24 a share.

Earlier this month, Hertz, benefiting from higher U.S. car rental revenues, posted record first quarter earnings of $19.7 million, compared to $8.8 million a year ago. Revenues were a record $878.4 million, compared to $803.1 million.
Ford has had an investment in Hertz since 1987, when it sought a captive customer for its excess vehicles. Three years ago, Ford took over all of Hertz.
